data.name: Snowflake's Chance
data.detailed_description:
You play as the hapless rabbit Snowflake. You have 99 chances to escape The Pit.

Every time you die the Evil Snowflake grows stronger.

Claw your way back up 21 brutal levels across a variety of areas. "Enlist" the help of other unfortunate critters to aid in your escape. You will need to run, dodge and hide from your enemies to make it through. You are weak and ineffectual!

Don’t slip! The Pit runs through the entire game so if you fall you might find yourself at the very bottom again.

Features:

- Uniquely terrifying: Every element of the game is hand-drawn and hand-animated offering a visceral, grittiness to every Chance you may squander.

- Listen to despair: The soundtrack is painstakingly crafted for the game, with iconic melodies that will stick in head long after you've rage quit! It is also available for download.

- You can run but you can't hide: Players must use their tactics and stealth to evade peril throughout the levels of The Pit, from the molten magma core to the dizzying vacuum of space.

- A Bunny's Arsenal: Snowflake isn't alone. Collecting Power-ups and insane items along the way may be your only chance to survive. A Crabbie Claw is essential to survival after all.

- Optimised for survival: The game is fully compatible with the Gamepad, so there's no excuse when you suck at it!

- Tread the unbeaten path: There is a plethora of secret routes, items and unmentionables to discover, if you're 'ard enough.

- As if it wasn't tough enough: There are 20 Steam achievements for you to master... or not.

- Some like it ridiculously hard: The level design is rigorously balanced to provide a real challenge, in the spirit of games like Oddworld: Abe’s Odyssey, Spelunky and Heart of Darkness.

data.short_description: A scurrying, scampering side-scroller. Run, dodge and hide from a menagerie of hand drawn nasties in this brutal indie platformer. You have 99 chances to escape The Pit. There is no hope.

reviews.review:
If you are reading this, you have found what I think is a hidden gem of the internet. Here is my opinion about it.

(Do not mouse over the spoilers if you wish to learn the game mechanics by yourself, as the game wants you to do)

[h1] Difficulty [/h1]

The game advertises itself as being very hard. It is.
This is really not for everyone. If you look at the achievements list, you will see that only 3 players have beaten the game completely out of 250 people. (At the moment I'm writing this). If you look for YouTube playthroughs, there aren't many in depth gameplay videos. This game likes to throw away an hour of hard work on a single miscalculation and then to rub it in your face. If you're looking for just something you will try "just for fun", then this is not the game for you.

You don't need to be amazing in gaming, you just need serious dedication. (about 30 hours to win if you have an average skill level like me and you go in blind, and perhaps 15 hours if you read guides and watch videos. Every run takes from 25 minutes to 1 hour and 30 minutes depending on your performance.)

One thing I didn't like is that you can only quit after you died if you don't want to lose your current life. That means that when you get good at the game, you need to keep going until you die in order to keep your items (which are destroyed upon death).


[h1] Gameplay	[/h1]


Overall, the game mechanics are really creative and interesting. You have two health points between life and death, and you lose everything on a simple mistake. The game rewards you for not dying by allowing you to take shortcuts. (Monkey and Crab statues). You can use various animals as distractions, ranged weaponry, death protection and more. Each one has a different effect. The game is heavily based on exploration, there are a lot of secrets and hidden shortcuts requiring specific animals.

Something I loved about the game is that you often have two ways to go, left and right, each one with different enemies and patterns. Pick the least difficult paths. There are also some hidden shortcuts and jumping tricks to avoid some very nasty areas.

You will find yourself going through diverse areas with special traits and mechanics unique to them such as [spoiler] a deadly fortress filled with traps, a space stage with low gravity and the Devil's lair. [/spoiler] Of course, if you rage quit early you'll never see any of this (this is likely to happen, you need to persevere for at least 1 hour until you start to make good progress).

[h1] Graphics [/h1]

As the title suggests, everything here is hand drawn in a style you can judge by looking at the screenshots. I personally like it but it's really up to you.

I love how decorative assets in the game are very rarely reused in the game: almost every statue, building, banner, plant, and the like are hand-drawn separately.

Everytime you die, a short gruesome death animation will occur. The most visually unsettling ones in my opinion are [spoiler] the "mind control owls", the chainsaws and the spike traps.[/spoiler]

[h1] Performance [/h1]

I had no FPS issues on a regular work laptop. You might experience some lag with older computers but everything seems to be fine.

I used a keyboard, which is quite responsive. Some said the controller controls are a bit off, but I think that's been fixed in 1.1.5.

[h1] Atmosphere and Music[/h1]

You play as a powerless rabbit in Hell. Enough said.

Not much to the story, you [spoiler]ate a cursed corn cob in the beginning of the game[/spoiler] and find yourself inside The Pit.

I liked how there's almost no text to read in the game besides item tooltips and tutorial signs. Everything is well written, when there is text.

The music is very good. Most tracks are not something you'd listen out of the game, but they set the mood very well. Some of the tracks are amazing and are definitly worth the 5$. Listen to the trailer to get a feel for it. I especially love the theme for the penultimate stage, "The Lower Gate".

[h1] Conclusion and Final Grade[/h1]

Overall I loved this game. I will keep playing it to achieve the  [spoiler] 'good ending', but the bad ending is still a very hard challenge.  EDIT: After some messing around with the karma system, I managed to reach the "good ending" and to complete a hidden challenge (Do No Harm) without even knowing it. Still need to do the rest of the achievements though...
SECOND EDIT: Thanks to the amazing guide by Poski, I managed to 100% the game 
 besides the One Chance achievement (I got close to getting it once by dying on the final boss, but I don't feel like doing it) and the Hell is Other Rabbits achievement (huge nope to that)[/spoiler]

Before you buy this, make sure you don't have any other uncompleted games waiting, as you will never beat Snowflake if you get distracted.

The game certainly knows very well how to build up tension. You will feel desperate at times, amazed at others, you will feel like something is impossible and one minute later you'll have done it. When you first start, getting through the first levels will be a great feat, but later on, it will become extremely easy. I loved how I managed to get my first win with only one chance/life left.

My final score is a 9/10. It's extremely unforgiving and seems like the game was never playtested when you start, but when you get the hang of it it's really fun to see so much progress being made. I probably [strike] squandered [/strike] used carefully over 1000 chances/lives, but it's worth it in the end for the satisfaction, which is a lot more than a simple "it's finally over".

Should you buy this game to prove your determination and your willpower to finish it?
If that sounds like your kind of game, go ahead. I think you should.

I recommend you look at some YouTube videos first. BubbleKnight has finished most of the game, which can help you get the hang of it. I didn't though, because there are some events in the game which should not be spoiled!

Good luck...

PS: Here is a link to an excellent (and humorous!) guide by Poski to this game. 
WARNING: Tons of spoilers.
